- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast marginally to account for downward momentum reversal.
- Model frequently overshoots after strong upward moves (e.g., >72.5) — cap forecast at +5–10% above peak if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33), model lags in correction — adjust forecast downward by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show high forecast vs low true, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until trend stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts — apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecast if sentiment volatility >0.5.
